review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked the WithGenericPoint and GenericFork usages across the formal-frontier libraries and searched Mathlib's Topology directory for an existing generic-point fork, a WithBot-style spectrum model or an Option-based specialization order. I found nothing. The deprecated Topology.GenericFork aliases forward to WithGenericPoint rather than defining a rival structure, and tests such as GenericForkCompatibility.lean exercise them for compatibility, so they are a deliberate migration shim. forkPoint and forkHomeomorph are new named maps between the fork and PrimeSpectrum, not duplicates of a Mathlib concept. PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_iff_eq_empty_or_bot_mem is a theorem, which is outside the rubric. The Finite instance for the spectrum is also a theorem-level fact, not a competing concept. I am fairly confident there is no justified finding; the remaining uncertainty is that I did not search all of Mathlib exhaustively.
